data.long_meaning: Teophila is a Greek name derived from the Greek words 'Theos' (God) and 'Philos' (loving). It was given to girls who were deeply devoted to God or to saints named after God. In Christianity, the name is associated with saints Teophila of Thessalonica and Teophila of Nicaea. The name Teophila carries the meaning “God-loving” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Teophila usually hope their child will grow to embody god-loving and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_greek.name: Θεοφίλα
in_greek.long_meaning: Θεοφίλα προέρχεται από τις λέξεις 'θεός' (Θεός) και 'φίλος' (φίλα), που σημαίνει φίλος του Θεού. Ο όρος χρησιμοποιείται στην Καινή Διαθήκη και συμβολίζει την αγάπη και τη φιλία προς τον Θεό

in_latin.name: Theophila

historical_references.reference: Teophila was a Christian martyr venerated in Sicily. She is believed to have lived during the 3rd century A.D. and was martyred during the Diocletian Persecution. According to legend, she was a young girl who was tortured and killed for refusing to renounce her faith in Christ.

Another Saint Teophila is known in the Eastern Orthodox Church. She is believed to have been a daughter of Theodosius the Great and a sister of Emperor Arcadius and Empress Pulcheria. She is venerated as a patron saint of Constantinople and is said to have dedicated her life to serving the poor and helping widows and orphans.
